market_context: Stocks are rallying hard on Monday after a rough post-election week. The Nasdaq fell into correction last week, and chips are rebounding (SOXX up about 7%). Oil is falling, and VIX is down 23% to 19.7. NVDA is the exception, down about 5% after its board opened a probe into CEO Jensen Huang. October CPI is due Tuesday, and the 10-year yield is near 4.86-4.88%, so some caution is likely into the close.

predictions.reasoning: SPY is trading within about $1 of its day high of $755.42 with only 20 minutes left, and the rally has built through the session. Breadth is broad and VIX has dropped sharply. A small drift higher into the close is slightly more likely than a fade, though the CPI release tomorrow could prompt some profit-taking.

QQQ is near its high of $681.70 after a gain of about 3.8%, led by semiconductors and mega-cap tech. The Nasdaq-100 is still down roughly 13% over the past month, so dip buyers have room to keep going into the close. Risk of a CPI-eve fade keeps confidence low.

NVDA bounced from a low of $170.24 to $177.37 and is the most oversold it has been since 2019, with short interest around 23%. Cantor and HSBC say the chip selloff is overdone. Late-day dip buying and short covering should give a small bounce, though the CEO probe headlines are still a risk.
